**Analysis of the test image:**

**Plant:** Banana (*Musa* sp.)

**Affected parts & visual features:**
- The whole plant crown is affected — leaves are tightly clustered and bunched together at the top
- Leaves appear shorter, more erect, and more rigid than normal banana leaves
- New emerging leaves in the center are packed tightly together
- A large older leaf on the left shows yellowing/chlorosis
- The plant has a distinctly compact, stunted appearance
- The pseudostem base shows some browning of outer sheaths

**Reasoning through the classes:**

- **Anthracnose**: Typically produces dark, sunken lesions on fruit — not seen here
- **Cigar End Rot**: Affects banana finger tips — no fruit present/affected
- **Cordana Leaf Spot**: Would show oval brown spots with yellow halos on leaves — not the pattern here
- **Yellow & Black Sigatoka**: Causes progressive leaf spotting with streaks/stripes — not the dominant symptom
- **Panama Disease**: Fusarium wilt causes progressive yellowing starting from outer/lower leaves, leaves droop and collapse around the pseudostem. The yellowing on the left leaf hints at this, but the plant structure doesn't match fully.
- **Bunchy Top**: Caused by Banana Bunchy Top Virus (BBTV) — hallmark symptoms are leaves becoming shorter and stiffer, standing more erect, packed tightly together at the crown giving the plant a "bunched" look, with chlorosis in older leaves. **This matches the image very well.**

The tight clustering of upright, shortened leaves at the crown, the stunted plant height, and the characteristic "bunched" crown appearance are classic indicators of Bunchy Top.
